ths.text: Xenagos is a satyr whose planeswalker spark ignites in the Bakkeia, and after leaving Theros he returns with a desire for power and resolves to enter the Therosian pantheon as a god.
He attacks Meletis, Akros and Setessa with otherworldly monsters, blinding the gods so that Kruphix enacts the Silence of the Gods.

During the siege of Akros he uses the victory celebration to stage the Great Revel, forcing the frenzied worship that lifts him to godhood as the god of revels, while Elspeth is scapegoated and exiled.
Elspeth and Ajani, aided by Nylea, finally confront him in Nyx, and Elspeth throws Godsend into his chest, detonating the arrowhead Nylea shot and killing him.

bng.text: Xenagos returns to Theros and performs rituals to become the god of revels, which blur the lines between Nyx and the mortal world and send Nyxborn pouring into it.

Elspeth leads heroes from Akros, Meletis and Setessa to break the siege, but the victory celebration becomes the ritual that launches Xenagos into Nyx as a god, and Elspeth is blamed and driven into the wilderness.
The gods realize a mortal has forced his way into the pantheon, and Kruphix later explains that Xenagos traveled to godless worlds and tried to show everyone the gods were a lie.

jou.text: Xenagos uses the Akroans' celebration after they defeat Mogis's minotaur horde to stage the final ritual that raises him to godhood, and the gods blame mortals and swear vengeance against human civilization.
His story began with Raissa, who chose not to abandon her horned son as most satyr women do, and the boy later pushed a council member's son to his death so they were cast out of Setessa.
Elspeth, supported by Ajani and armed with Godsend, faces Xenagos on his home ground in Nyx and kills him, and his disciple Guruthes mourns that the world grows dark without him.
